item.diagram_kind: Markov stabilization of a one-strand unknot braid
item.selection_reason: The example compares closure before and after a ± stabilization, a concrete diagrammatic instance of Markov equivalence.
item.concrete_diagram_content_or_checks: Draw the closure of the identity 1-braid and the closure of its positive/negative stabilization in B₂; verify both are unknots and that strand count increases by one, with generator sign matching source.

source_lines.41: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The trivial braid $e\in B_1$ closes to the unknot, and both stabilizations
source_lines.42: $e\sigma_1$ and $e\sigma_1^{-1}$ in $B_2$ also close to the unknot; the explicit
source_lines.43: isotopies are the R1 unwinding of the added kink, one for each sign. Here the
source_lines.44: **unknot** is the closure of the trivial one-strand braid.
